quote: I've heard both both stories. So what got what got me, what caught my attention under your ad is, it says solar, no cost, and you get a, Tesla Powerwall, and stuff like that.
stewart_read: Customer discloses he already has quotes from multiple companies AND cites a specific ad promise (free Powerwall). The rep never asks which companies or what those competitors offered, losing competitive intel the closer could use.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be deliberately avoiding a scope-creep rabbit hole by not chasing competitor details mid-qualification.
coaching_implication: Coach a 15-second probe: 'Which companies did you talk to, and did they mention a Powerwall too?' — cheap intel for the closer, doesn't require the rep to answer anything technical.

quote: it says solar, no cost, and you get a, Tesla Powerwall, and stuff like that.
stewart_read: Customer is anchored on a specific marketed promise — a free Powerwall — which is a real Ion offering (the only battery brand Ion carries) but nothing in the call confirms or scopes that expectation for the closer. The rep's later deferral at 02:00 addresses PPA vs. purchase generally but never separately flags the battery expectation as its own line item.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep's general deferral ('I'll write that down') may already implicitly cover the Powerwall question, making a separate flag redundant.
coaching_implication: Have the rep explicitly note in the handoff that the customer is expecting a Powerwall to be part of the no-cost offer — the closer needs to confirm or correct that specific expectation, not just the PPA-vs-loan question generally.

quote: I I like paying for what I consume, and I guess whatever, you know, delivery fee they're charging should be included already in the rate that you're selling them exclusively at.
stewart_read: Customer is talking himself through whether solar will actually lower his bill, given that delivery fees (not usage) drive his cost — this is exactly the moment to flip the fixed-fee pain into a reason solar still helps usage-based charges, but the rep says nothing and lets the customer keep reasoning out loud alone.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be intentionally letting the customer self-resolve rather than interject, since the customer appears to talk himself back to acceptance ('I gotta pay regardless. Right?').
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to briefly validate and reframe here: acknowledge delivery fees are fixed, but usage-based charges are what solar reduces, tying back to his stated efficiency goal — a live curiosity-building opening that went unused.

quote: But I'm not interested in the PPA at all. That's that's just like, you can put that in the notes as well.
stewart_read: This is a stated financing-structure preference, not a cost/time/interest objection — the customer isn't objecting to solar, he's pre-filtering which offer structure he'll accept. The rep correctly logs it for the notes rather than trying to talk him out of his preference.
coaching_implication: Confirm this preference makes it verbatim into the handoff brief — if the closer opens with a PPA pitch, the appointment is at risk before it starts.

quote: we've managed to get it down a little bit because we insulated. Like I said, we've been, like, working on getting, like, the the home as energy efficient as possible.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers that he's actively invested time and money into efficiency upgrades — a signal of a highly engaged, detail-oriented homeowner who cares about optimizing usage, which the rep could anchor future conversation on.
coaching_implication: This kind of proactive-efficiency customer is a strong closer fit; flag in the handoff that he's already made efficiency investments and will likely want precise usage-based numbers, not a generic pitch.

quote: Are you able to email me the sign and, like, the cost and everything before that the representative would show up?
stewart_read: This is the send-proposal-before-meeting hard rule. The rep doesn't cave — he says he can't access it and would have to check policy — which lands close to the correct hold, but he never gives the clean, confident scripted line ('we don't email proposals because they need full explanation') and instead sounds uncertain about why.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep's hedged 'I don't know for sure what their policy is' could read as weak rather than a genuine hold of the rule.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to replace 'I don't know for sure what their policy is' with the confident scripted reason — proposals require walkthrough to make sense — so the hold sounds like policy, not uncertainty.

quote: is there anybody else in the title of the home with you, or is it just you?
stewart_read: Rep asks the co-owner question correctly and gets 'my wife too,' but never follows up to get her onto the Tuesday appointment or ask about her schedule directly — he only later hears secondhand that scheduling both of them together is hard.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be treating the later scheduling comment ('my wife and I have automated schedules, hard to get us both') as sufficient acknowledgment without needing a direct ask.
coaching_implication: Coach a direct follow-up at the moment the wife is identified: 'Great, let's make sure she's able to join Tuesday too' — right now the appointment is booked with only the husband confirmed.
